text:
opsbot: INCIDENT PAGE: Possible cross-tenant KV-cache read detected in Dedicated pool 'd-pool-7' affecting customer SolaceCorp (VPC). Alert: 6 anomalous fetches from tenant workspace IDs mapped to both SolaceCorp and another tenant. Paging on-call.

sara: oncall here (sara) — looking now. pulling logs for d-pool-7. ping @mike for infra help and @emily for CS/customer contact.

mike: on it. grabbing pod placements and routing tables. any packet captures available from the time window? timestamp window @opsbot?

opsbot: Alert window: 2026-03-15T03:12:04Z -> 2026-03-15T03:14:28Z. Example request ids: r_8f3a2b, r_8f3a6d, r_8f3a90.

sara: thanks. initial query looks like prefix routing overlap between dedicated pool allocator and VPC overlay. repeating: this is suspected KV prefix collision, not model output data exfil yet. need containment.

raj: I see two allocations for d-pool-7 where tenant prefix map includes a legacy route for customer-502 that was supposed to be retired. looks like a stale route in route-indexer. pulling indexer logs.

mike: can we cordon d-pool-7? i.e., stop new connections and prevent new KV attach ops while we scrub routing? suggested command:

mike: ```
# cordon pool (dry-run -> force)
redwoodctl pool cordon d-pool-7 --mode=evict-attach
``` 

sara: agree. do cordon now. will also bump traffic to fallback pool for SolaceCorp.

emily: FYI I've opened a high-priority support thread with SolaceCorp (cust-eng-julian). telling them we're investigating possible routing artifact. no confirmed data exposure. i'll keep them updated every 30m.

sara: cordon issued at 03:20Z. command output: "cordon scheduled, active connections allowed to finish (120s), new KV attaches rejected". also enabled read-only routing for existing sessions.

raj: indexer logs show a reconciliation job failed on 2026-03-15T02:59Z during a prior rollout; patch revert left a shadow mapping: prefix "/kv/solace/" was present in both tenant map and a deprecated shared namespace. looks like the recon sync didn't clear stale entries.

mike: confirmed. list of affected prefixes (sample):

mike: ```
/kv/solace/llm-cache
/kv/solace/session-meta
/kv/solace/prompt-anchors
``` 

sara: risk assessment: if a cross-read occurred, the attacker would only have been able to GET cached keys; writes not likely. we should assume any GET could contain PII depending on customer usage. classify as potential data exposure until verified.

emily: telling cust-eng-julian that we are treating as potential exposure. customer asked for ETA — can we give a 90m timeline for root cause + mitigation steps? they're pushing for a quick standup.

mike: next steps:
1) scrub indexer and remove stale mappings (safe-plan below)
2) run KV read diff to detect cross-tenant reads
3) rotate pool-level access tokens if we see unauthorized GETs
4) coordinate for a customer notification template

raj: starting step 1 now. plan: run targeted reconciliation only for d-pool-7, for prefixes with last changed < 2026-03-14. command:

raj: ```
redwoodctl index reconcile --pool d-pool-7 --prefix-filter "/kv/solace/" --dry-run
redwoodctl index reconcile --pool d-pool-7 --prefix-filter "/kv/solace/" --apply
``` 

sara: run dry-run first and paste output here. don't apply without approval.

raj: dry-run output (excerpt): "found stale mapping id s-0912 -> shared-legacy-ns for /kv/solace/llm-cache; would remove mapping; impact estimate: 0 writes, 12 recent reads by tenant SolaceCorp; 3 reads attributed to tenant 'gamma-ops' (potential cross-read)."

sara: thanks. approve apply. we need evidence collection before we delete — capture full GET request traces for those three reads and preserve chain ids.

mike: created forensics snapshot: `forensics/d-pool-7/2026-03-15--0315.tar.gz` and uploaded to secure bucket. commands used:

mike: ```
redwoodctl forensics snapshot --pool d-pool-7 --window "2026-03-15T03:10:00Z/2026-03-15T03:20:00Z" --ids r_8f3a2b,r_8f3a6d,r_8f3a90
# uploaded -> s3://redwood-forensics/prod/evidence/2026-03-15/d-pool-7/
``` 

sara: good. proceed with apply. raj please run apply and confirm.

raj: apply started at 03:36Z. indexer logs show removal of stale mapping succeeded. route-index cache invalidated, and route-service restarted gracefully.

opsbot: SYSTEM: route-indexer reconciliation completed for d-pool-7 at 2026-03-15T03:38:02Z.

mike: post-apply checks: running KV read diff to see whether any keys were read by wrong tenant. command:

mike: ```
redwoodctl kv diff --pool d-pool-7 --prefix "/kv/solace/" --window "2026-03-15T03:10:00Z/2026-03-15T03:40:00Z"
``` 

mike: diff output (summary): "12 reads by SolaceCorp, 3 reads by gamma-ops referencing same key hashes -> cross-tenant read signatures match. full traces in forensics bundle."

sara: that's unfortunate. next: rotate pool-level access tokens and rotate any KV-level creds for affected keys. set token rotation expiry immediate for d-pool-7.

mike: token rotation command run at 03:45Z: `redwoodctl tokens rotate --pool d-pool-7 --force`. new tokens issued; old tokens invalidated after 30s.

emily: telling cust-eng-julian now: we confirmed a limited set of GETs that likely exposed cached keys; we've rotated tokens and isolated the pool. offering detailed forensics and remediation steps; customer asked for a copy of the diffs and timeline.

sara: prepare customer-facing summary + technical appendix. include: timeline, what happened, actions taken (cordon, indexer fix, token rotate), impact (3 cross-tenant GETs, potential PII), mitigation (rotation + replayable checks), and follow-ups.

emily: draft posted to support thread, flagged legal/compliance. cust-eng-julian: "we appreciate the quick action, want to know if user data was in the keys" — we'll follow after KV content review.

raj: spinning up content audit job to look inside cached keys for matching SolaceCorp identifiers (hashed/email patterns). will do in secure forensics environment; output will be internal-only.

mike: after audit we'll mark incident severity and recommended customer notification level. current recommended: SEV-2 (customer-sensitive exposure) and notify affected customer with offer of data extract and support. also recommend warming plan for dedicated pool reconciles.

opsbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: containment achieved at 2026-03-15T03:46Z. Cordon active, stale mappings removed, tokens rotated.

sara: handoff to post-incident team: @oncall-postmortem please pick this up for RCA and follow-ups. key owners: raj (indexer), mike (tokens/forensics), emily (customer comms).

oncall-postmortem: acknowledged. creating postmortem ticket PM-2026-345 and scheduling 60m RCA. please attach forensics bundle and diff output.

emily: scheduling customer sync for 03:00Z+2h as requested. will share timeline and next steps.

sara: final note: we should add a safe-guard to reconciler to fail-open vs fail-stale-policy — follow-up item in RCA. closing page for now, but keep channel open for any new evidence.

cust-eng-julian: (via support thread) thanks team. we will review internal keys and let you know if we see user identifiers. please keep us posted.

mike: leaving diagnostic watch on d-pool-7 for 24h. will elevate if any anomalous reads appear.

sara: last message here at 03:49Z. closing thread for live mitigation. documented evidence in PM-2026-345.
